sections.title: PRINCETON ISD GREEN CORD COMMUNITY SERVICE PROGRAM HANDBOOK

blocks.text: The Princeton ISD Green Cord Community Service Program recognizes students who demonstrate a commitment to serving others through meaningful volunteer work within their school and community.
The program is designed to encourage students to develop a lifelong habit of service while building leadership skills, civic responsibility, and community involvement.
Students may begin earning hours on June 1 prior to their freshman year and continue accumulating hours through their senior year.
Students who complete the required service hours will receive recognition based upon their grade level participation and may ultimately earn the prestigious Green Cord to wear at graduation.

blocks.text: The purpose of the Princeton ISD Green Cord Community Service Program is to:
Encourage community engagement and civic responsibility.
Recognize students who make a positive impact on others.
Foster partnerships between Princeton ISD and the surrounding community.
Help students build experiences that strengthen college, military, trade school, and
Inspire students to become lifelong servants and leaders.

sections.title: PROGRAM PURPOSE

blocks.text: Students interested in participating in the Princeton ISD Green Cord Community Service Program must complete the enrollment process each school year by October 1 to be eligible for annual recognition and awards.
To become a Green Cord member, students must:
Complete the Green Cord Membership Application
Submit the Parent & Student Acknowledgement Form
Pay the one-time $20 Green Cord Membership Fee
Join the Green Cord Google Classroom
Once all enrollment requirements have been completed, students may begin submitting eligible community service hours for verification.
Students are encouraged to enroll as early as possible to maximize volunteer opportunities throughout the school year.

sections.title: HOW TO JOIN THE PROGRAM

blocks.text: A one-time membership fee of $20.00 is required upon enrollment in the Princeton ISD Green Cord Community Service Program. Payable through RevTrak.
The membership fee helps cover program expenses including:

Annual service certificates Recognition materials and awards Printing and program administration Senior recognition activities Students pay the membership fee only once during their high school career.
Membership remains active through graduation provided the student remains enrolled in Princeton ISD.

blocks.text: The Green Cord Program operates on an annual basis. Service hours do not carry over from one school year to the next.
Each school year begins with a zero-hour balance. Students must earn the required number of service hours during that school year to qualify for recognition.
Students may begin earning hours for the upcoming school year on June 1 preceding that academic year.
Minimum 25 cumulative verified service hours Recognition:
Minimum 50 cumulative verified service hours Recognition:
Minimum 75 cumulative verified service hours Recognition:
Minimum 100 cumulative verified service hours Recognition:
If a student completes all four years they would complete a total of 250 hours.

sections.title: FOUR-YEAR SERVICE DISTINCTION

blocks.text: Princeton ISD recognizes that some students may transfer into the district after freshman year and that students graduating prior to the Class of 2030 did not have access to the Green Cord Program during all four years of high school.

To provide equitable access to the Princeton ISD Distinguished Service Scholar designation while preserving the prestige of the award, alternative pathways have been established for transfer students and founding classes.

sections.title: Founding Classes Provision

blocks.text: Students who transfer into Princeton High School after their freshman year may qualify for the Princeton ISD Distinguished Service Scholar designation by meeting the service-hour requirements for their applicable pathway. Because transfer students have fewer years available to participate in the Green Cord Program, they must complete a greater number of service hours during the years they are eligible to participate in order to demonstrate a comparable level of sustained service.

The Distinguished Service Scholar pathway is separate from the senior-year Distinguished Service Levels. A transfer student's senior-year cord recognition is determined solely by the number of verified service hours completed during senior year.
Students transferring into Princeton High School after freshman year may qualify for the Distinguished Service Scholar designation by meeting the following requirements:
Grade Level Hours Required Sophomore Year 75 Hours Junior Year 75 Hours Senior Year 100 Hours Minimum Total: 250 Hours
Grade Level Hours Required Junior Year 100 Hours Senior Year 150 Hours Minimum Total: 250 Hours

Grade Level Hours Required Senior Year 250 Hours Minimum Total: 250 Hours Any student who meets this requirement and maintains compliance with all Green Cord Program requirements will qualify for the Princeton ISD Distinguished Service Scholar designation.

sections.title: Transfer Student Distinguished Service Scholar Pathway

blocks.text: Transfer students remain eligible for the same senior-year service recognitions as all other Princeton High School students. The number of hours required for each senior-year distinction does not change based on when a student enters the district.

Green Cord 100–149 senior-year hours Silver Service Distinction 150–199 senior-year hours Gold Service Distinction 200+ senior-year hours Students earning Silver or Gold Service Distinction will be recognized during the Senior Awards Program.

Important: Earning a Green, Silver, or Gold senior-year distinction does not automatically qualify a transfer student for the Distinguished Service Scholar designation. The Distinguished Service Scholar designation requires completion of the applicable transfer pathway and the required cumulative service hours.
Transfer students must enroll in the Green Cord Program during their first eligible year at Princeton High School and maintain compliance with all program requirements.
The Green Cord Coordinator and campus administration reserve the right to review unique enrollment circumstances and make final determinations regarding eligibility.

sections.title: WHAT COUNTS AS COMMUNITY SERVICE

blocks.text: To encourage a variety of service experiences, the following limits apply.
Maximum: 40 hours Students must complete service through at least three separate organizations before qualifying for the Green Cord Award during their Senior Year.

sections.plainText: To encourage a variety of service experiences, the following limits apply. School-Based Service Maximum: 60 hours Examples: Teacher assistance outside school hours Campus beautification School-sponsored service projects Academic tutoring Faith Based Organizations Maximum: 40 hours Examples: Food pantry assistance Community outreach events Faith based agency event volunteering Childcare during events Clothing drives Mission service activities Single Organization Limit Maximum: 40 hours Students must complete service through at least three separate organizations before qualifying for the Green Cord Award during their Senior Year.
sections.title: SERVICE HOUR LIMITATIONS

blocks.text: The following activities are not eligible for Green Cord credit:
Babysitting for individuals or family members
Activities completed solely for a grade
Community service for truancy or probation requirements

sections.plainText: The following activities are not eligible for Green Cord credit: Paid employment Internships receiving compensation Babysitting for individuals or family members Household chores Yard work for family members Caring for siblings Activities completed solely for a grade Mandatory club service requirements Athletic team obligations Club meetings Fundraising sales Donation collection Travel time during service trips Sleeping hours during service trips Recreational activities during service trips Community service for truancy or probation requirements Court ordered community service

sections.title: PARENT RESPONSIBILITIES

blocks.text: Q: Can I earn hours during the summer?
A: Yes. Hours may begin June 1 before freshman year and reset on June 1st for each school year.
Q: Can I count NHS hours?
A: Only if the hours are not required for membership.
Q: Can I count mission trips?
A: Actual service hours only. Travel, worship, and recreation time do not count.
Q: Can family members sign my form?
Q: What if I am unsure whether an activity qualifies?
A: Contact your counselor or Green Cord Coordinator before participating.
Q: I joined and filled out all the membership forms during my sophomore year, do I have to fill it out again during my junior year?
A: No, once you join you remain a member and active as long as you are enrolled in PISD.
